- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is rising, model underestimates continuation — add 2–5% to forecast if trend persists.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment < 0.2.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–3 days — if sentiment is trending, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.8), model fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 5–8% immediately after reversal.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model overpredicts recovery — cap forecast at 1–2% above prior low.
